symptom: The rebuilt backend cannot become healthy because MySQL rejects the configured application user.
evidence: Backend reports ER_ACCESS_DENIED_ERROR while establishing its TypeORM connection.
Frontend rebuilt successfully, is healthy and serves a bundle without UC-01 registration strings.

root_cause.summary: The credential stored for the application user in the persistent MySQL volume does not match the credential supplied to the rebuilt backend from the current environment file.

actions_attempted: Rebuilt and recreated the Compose stack without deleting the MySQL volume.
Started the rebuilt frontend without dependencies so the rolled-back UI is available.
Verified frontend reachability and absence of UC-01 registration strings in the served bundle.
Stopped database and backend, then ran MySQL locally through its Unix socket in temporary skip-grant-tables and skip-networking recovery mode.
Changed only the application-user password to the current environment value and restarted the normal database/backend services.
Verified database, backend and frontend health plus backend/frontend reachability.
reusable_resolution: With researcher authorization, stop database consumers, start MySQL temporarily with grant tables disabled and networking disabled, change only the application-user password to the current environment value through the local Unix socket, then restart and verify the normal stack. No volume deletion is required.
prevention: Keep the environment credential stable for the lifetime of the persistent MySQL volume, or rotate the database user credential before changing the environment file.
